commitResults.messageTitle: Add PersonId value class for persistent contact IDs
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce an immutable PersonId representing IDs of the form C<n>,
where n is a positive integer without leading zeros. Lowercase
prefixes, zero, negative numbers, missing numbers, unrelated text and
values that overflow an int are rejected.

IDs compare by numeric value, so C2 orders before C10.

PersonId is not yet attached to Person or used by any command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Assign persistent IDs to persons in memory
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit and delete currently pick a person by their position in the
displayed list, which changes whenever the list is filtered, sorted or
modified. To move to a stable reference such as C42, every person
first needs an ID that the system assigns and that never changes. This
commit gives each person such an ID while the app is running. Saving
IDs, showing them and targeting persons by ID come in later commits.

Person
- Add an optional PersonId. A person built from user input or sample
  data has no ID yet; the address book assigns one when it is added.
- Add a constructor that takes an ID, and getId() returning
  Optional<PersonId>. There is no setter, so an ID cannot be changed
  once set.
- Include the ID in equals(), hashCode() and toString(), so that a
  replacement person with a different ID no longer counts as equal.
  isSamePerson() still compares names only and continues to be used
  for duplicate detection.

AddressBook
- Keep a nextPersonId counter, starting at 1. ID allocation lives here
  rather than in parsers or commands, so users never supply an ID.
- addPerson() and setPersons() give each person without an ID the next
  number. A person that already has an ID keeps it, and the counter
  moves past it. The counter only advances once the person is accepted,
  so a rejected duplicate does not use up a number.
- Since the counter only moves forward, deleting a person never frees
  their ID for reuse.
- resetData() and the copy constructor carry the counter over. This is
  needed because ModelManager copies the initial address book, and
  without the counter newly added persons would reuse existing IDs.
- setPerson() rejects a replacement whose ID differs from the original,
  so no edit, current or future, can change a person's ID.
- Include the counter in equals(), hashCode() and toString().

ReadOnlyAddressBook
- Add getNextPersonId() so the counter is part of an address book's
  readable state, for copying now and for saving later.

EditCommand
- The edited person is built with the original person's ID. The
  descriptor of editable fields has no ID field, so the ID can only be
  kept, never edited.

Tests
- PersonBuilder can set an ID. TypicalPersons ALICE to GEORGE get
  C1 to C7, matching the order getTypicalAddressBook() adds them, while
  HOON, IDA, AMY and BOB stay without an ID as new persons to be added.
- Add tests for ID assignment order, keeping given IDs, not reusing
  deleted IDs, copying the counter, rejecting ID changes and editing
  keeping the ID.
- IDs are not saved to the data file yet, so reloading assigns them
  afresh. JsonAdaptedPersonTest and part of the
  JsonAddressBookStorageTest round trip temporarily compare persons
  without IDs until IDs are persisted.

Known limitation: clear still resets the counter to 1. Keeping the
counter across clear will be handled together with persistence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Make sure every changed line in AddressBook and Person is tested
commitResults.messageBody:
The code-coverage check on the previous pull request flagged a few lines
that no test ever ran. This fixes them.

AddressBook
- A safety check (an assert) inside the ID-counting helper could never
  fail, because a person always gets an ID just before it runs. A check
  that can never fail can never be tested, so it was flagged. The helper
  now receives the ID directly, and the check is no longer needed. The
  app behaves exactly as before.

Tests
- hashCode() in AddressBook and Person was never called by any test.
  These methods must stay: Java requires two equal objects to give the
  same hash code, or sets and maps would quietly misbehave. New tests
  check that equal objects produce equal hash codes.
- Add a test that an address book equals itself, does not equal null,
  and does not equal an unrelated object. These cases were never tested
  in the original AB3 code.

This fix missed the merge of PR #58, so it is included here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Save contact IDs so they survive restarts and are never reused
commitResults.messageBody:
Until now, contact IDs only existed while the app was running. When the
app closed, the IDs were not written to the save file, so every launch
numbered the contacts C1, C2, C3... again. After a deletion, a contact
could come back with a different ID, and a deleted contact's ID could be
handed to someone new.

This change writes the IDs to the save file and reads them back, so a
contact keeps the same ID for its whole lifetime.

What the save file now contains
- Each contact has an "id" field, e.g. "id": "C3".
- The file stores "nextPersonId", the number the next new contact will
  get. This counter has to be saved rather than worked out from the
  remaining contacts. Otherwise, deleting the highest-numbered contact
  (say C3) would make the app hand out C3 again.

Loading the save file (JsonAdaptedPerson, JsonSerializableAddressBook)
- Saved IDs and the counter are restored exactly as they were.
- Clearly broken data is rejected, like any other invalid field: two
  contacts sharing an ID, an invalid ID such as "c1", or a counter
  below 1.
- Data that is off but fixable is repaired safely. If the counter is
  not above the highest saved ID, it is raised past it. Contacts without
  an ID get new numbers above every ID already used. No existing ID is
  ever reused.

Upgrading old save files (JsonAddressBookStorage)
- Files saved before this feature have no IDs. When such a file is
  loaded, contacts are numbered C1, C2, ... in file order, and the file
  is saved again right away so these IDs are kept from then on.
- If that save fails, a warning is logged and the contacts still load,
  so a failed upgrade never leaves the user with an empty list.

Clearing the list (ClearCommand, AddressBook)
- clear still removes every contact, but now keeps the counter. If the
  list went up to C7, the next contact after clearing is C8, not C1.
- AddressBook gets a constructor for an empty address book that starts
  counting from a given number. Both loading and clear use it.

Tests
- Storage tests that ignored IDs while IDs were not saved now check
  them again.
- The sample save file used in tests now includes IDs and the counter.
- New sample files and tests cover: an old file without IDs, a deleted
  highest ID, a counter that is too low, a mix of contacts with and
  without IDs, duplicate IDs and an invalid counter. Other new tests
  check that old files are upgraded on disk, that a failed upgrade still
  loads the contacts, and that clear followed by add does not reuse IDs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Show contact IDs on cards and in command results
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts have had permanent IDs since the last two changes, but users
could not see them anywhere in the app. Before commands can target a
contact by ID, users need to know what each contact's ID is. This change
makes the ID visible. Commands still use list numbers for now.

Contact cards (PersonListCard.fxml, PersonCard, DarkTheme.css)
- Each card shows a small "ID: C1" tag on the same row as the name.
- The tag has its own gold, outlined style, so it is clearly different
  from the list number (1., 2., ...) and from the blue tags. The list
  number stays for now and is removed in a later change.
- The tag reads the ID from the contact itself, so it does not change
  when the list is searched or a contact is edited.

Result messages (Messages, AddCommand)
- Results for add, edit and delete now name the contact's ID right after
  the name, e.g. "New person added: Amy Bee (ID: C8); Phone: ...".
  All three use Messages.format, so the ID is added there once.
- add used to build its message from the contact before it was stored,
  when it did not have an ID yet. It now uses the stored contact.

Model (Model, ModelManager, AddressBook)
- addPerson now returns the contact as stored, with its new ID, so that
  add can show it. Callers that do not need it can ignore it.

Tests
- add tests expect the ID in the result message.
- New MessagesTest checks the message format with and without an ID.
- New checks that addPerson returns the stored contact with its ID.
- The line in PersonCard that sets the tag text is not covered, as AB3
  has no tests that draw the screen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
